source.version: Journal version of record: AI (MDPI) 2025, 6, 247, https://doi.org/10.3390/ai6100247; received 20 July 2025, revised 30 August 2025, accepted 16 September 2025, published 1 October 2025 (p. 1)
source.title_on_document: Creativeable: Leveraging AI for Personalized Creativity Enhancement

supplement.holds: Text S1 (prompt that generated the word triplets), Text S2 (prompt for feedback and difficulty adjustment), Text S3 (prompt that rated story creativity), Text S4 (reflection questions), Table S1 (word triplets with semantic distance and difficulty ratings), Table S2 (examples of improvement suggestions). The listing names no additional statistics; all test statistics used here are in the main text.

paper_design_summary: 385 Prolific participants (native English speakers aged 18-45) were placed in one of four conditions of an AI creativity-training tool, Creativeable, crossing GPT-4 feedback after each story (yes/no) with GPT-4-adjusted versus constant task difficulty, and wrote five short stories from three-word prompts. Conditions were filled by four separate recruitment batches, one per condition; the paper does not state random assignment. Creativity was scored with the Alternative Uses Task (originality scored by OCSAI, plus fluency) before and after training without the tool, and each training story was rated for creativity by GPT-4.

studies.label: Creativeable training experiment (four conditions, story writing; AUT pre and post)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Training condition: F/VL (GPT-4 feedback, AI-adjusted difficulty), F/CL (GPT-4 feedback, constant difficulty), NF/VL (no feedback, AI-adjusted difficulty), NF/CL (no feedback, constant difficulty). Each condition was filled by its own recruitment batch.
assignment.quote: Recruitment was conducted in four separate batches, each corresponding to one of the study's experimental conditions, to ensure smooth operation of the study platform.
assignment.locator: p. 6, Section 2.1 Participants; also p. 23, Section 4.5 Limitations ("Data collection in separate batches raises potential concerns about temporal differences")

arms.name: F/VL
arms.description: GPT-4 'creativity trainer' gives general feedback and one improvement suggestion after each of five story rounds, and adjusts word-triplet difficulty each round based on performance and self-reported fatigue.

arms.name: F/CL
arms.description: Same GPT-4 feedback and suggestions as F/VL; difficulty stays fixed at medium-easy across the five rounds.

arms.name: NF/VL
arms.description: No feedback; the GPT-4 trainer adjusts task difficulty each round based on performance and fatigue. Participants see no AI-written content.

arms.name: NF/CL
arms.description: Control condition: no feedback and constant (medium-easy) difficulty; five story rounds with no AI involvement visible to the participant.

participants.exclusions: Participants were excluded if they did not complete the study, gave overly brief responses, or completed the tasks unusually quickly (p. 6). The number excluded is not stated; 385 is the count included in the study.
participants.who: Prolific workers, native English speakers aged 18-45 with at least 12 years of formal education; paid 9 GBP per hour. Mean age 28.8-31.7 by condition (Table 1).
participants.quote: A total of 385 participants were included in the study, recruited via the crowdsourcing platform Prolific.
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 2.1 and Table 1 (N: F/VL 97, F/CL 98, NF/VL 93, NF/CL 97)

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT-4 via API (the 'AI trainer'); GPT-4 also rated story creativity, and OCSAI (a prompted GPT model) scored AUT originality
ai_tool.how_used: After each submitted story, the feedback arms received two sentences of general feedback on that story and one suggestion for improving creativity or brainstorming in the next round (p. 9, Section 2.2.7). Feedback came after the story was submitted; participants did not revise it, and the AI wrote no story content. In the VL arms GPT-4 also chose whether to raise, keep, or lower the difficulty of the next word triplet (p. 9, Section 2.2.6). The AI comments on the person's own story, so 'refinement' also partly fits.

task.description: Training task: five rounds of the Story Writing Task, writing a 60-80-word story that uses three given words. Pre/post assessment: two Alternative Uses Task items before and two after training (2 minutes each), plus an animal Semantic Fluency Task as a non-creative control.
task.duration: Whole study about 50 minutes on average (p. 10, Section 2.5)

outcomes.name: AUT originality after training (OCSAI score, 1-5)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: OCSAI online platform (prompted GPT) scores each use 1-5; averaged within item, then across the two post-training items (p. 10, Section 2.3). Also reported as percent improvement from pre to post per participant, and as a time x condition mixed ANOVA.
outcomes.delay: Same session, right after the five training rounds

contrasts.reported: Post-training AUT: F/CL M = 2.81 (SD = 0.38), n = 98 vs NF/CL M = 2.84 (SD = 0.35), n = 97; pre-training F/CL 2.56 (0.40), NF/CL 2.63 (0.37). One-way ANOVA on post-training scores F(3, 381) = 3.34, p = 0.002, eta^2 = 0.025; Tukey HSD: only NF/VL vs F/VL significant, other pairs not significant. Percent improvement: F/CL M = 11.6%, SD = 17.42%, 95%CI = [8.11, 15.09] vs NF/CL M = 9.42%, SD = 15.0%, 95%CI = [6.41, 12.44]; ANOVA F(3, 381) = 3.12, p = 0.025; no significant difference between these two.
contrasts.locator: pp. 13-14, Section 3.2.1 and Figure 3 (p. 14); Table 1 (p. 6) for n

contrasts.reported: Post-training AUT: F/VL M = 2.71 (SD = 0.44), n = 97 vs NF/CL M = 2.84 (SD = 0.35), n = 97; pre F/VL 2.60 (0.34). Tukey HSD on post-training scores: not significant. Percent improvement F/VL M = 4.82%, SD = 16.2%, 95%CI = [1.57, 8.09] vs NF/CL 9.42% [6.41, 12.44]; no significant difference.

Post-training AUT: NF/VL M = 2.89 (SD = 0.41), n = 93 vs NF/CL M = 2.84 (SD = 0.35), n = 97; pre NF/VL 2.67 (0.33). Tukey HSD: not significant. Percent improvement NF/VL M = 8.61%, SD = 14.14%, 95%CI = [5.7, 11.52] vs NF/CL 9.42%; no significant difference.

Tukey HSD on post-training AUT: significant mean difference between NF/VL and F/VL (DeltaM = 0.175, SE = 0.06, p = 0.014, Cohen's d = 0.41); post means F/VL 2.71 (0.44) vs NF/VL 2.89 (0.41). Percent improvement: F/CL vs F/VL mean difference 6.77%, SE = 2.25, p = 0.015, d = 0.4 (the only significant pair for improvement rates).

outcomes.name: AUT fluency after training (number of uses)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of uses per item, averaged over the two post-training items (p. 10, Section 2.3).

contrasts.reported: Mixed ANOVA on number of AUT responses: time F(1, 381) = 0.04, p = 0.90, eta^2 = 0.0; time x condition F(3, 381) = 1.53, p = 0.2, eta^2 = 0.01. Arm means shown only in Figure 4 (bars about 6.2-7.2).

outcomes.name: GPT-4-rated creativity of training stories (1-5), by round
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4 prompted as a creative-writing expert rated each story 1-5 on imagination, surprise, originality, and integration of the three words; each story rated five times and averaged (pp. 8-9, Section 2.2.5). Stories in VL arms used harder word triplets in later rounds, so difficulty differs by arm.

contrasts.reported: Condition x round mixed ANOVA: condition F(3, 381) = 29.48, p < 0.001, eta^2 = 0.155; round F(4, 1524) = 10.21, p < 0.001, eta^2 = 0.026; interaction F(12, 1524) = 2.01, p = 0.02, eta^2 = 0.016. Arm means and between-arm post hoc tests are not printed, so the direction between arms is not given. Within-arm: F/VL F(4, 384) = 3.32, p = 0.01, round 1 M = 2.7 (SD = 0.6) to round 3 M = 2.98 (SD = 0.79), t(96) = 3.12, p = 0.02, d = 0.38; F/CL F(4, 388) = 12.14, p < 0.001, eta^2 = 0.058, round 1 M = 3.03 (0.66) to round 3 M = 3.49 (0.69), t(97) = 5.52, d = 0.43, to round 5 M = 3.44 (0.75), t(97) = 4.97, d = 0.57; NF arms no significant change (all p's > 0.05).

outcomes.name: Semantic Fluency Task (animals) responses after training (non-creative control task)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of animals named in 2 minutes (p. 10, Section 2.4). The paper uses it as a non-creative control task, so it answers none of the three questions.

contrasts.reported: Mixed ANOVA: time F(1, 381) = 0.40, p = 0.52, eta^2 = 0.001; time x condition F(3, 381) = 0.29, p = 0.83, eta^2 = 0.002; condition F(3, 381) = 5.0, p = 0.01, eta^2 = 0.04. Means only in Figure 5.

company_involvement.description: No external funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest. GPT-4 used as the tool, not a company partner.
company_involvement.locator: p. 25, Funding and Conflicts of Interest

eligibility.reason: Conditions were filled by four separate recruitment batches, one per condition (p. 6; p. 23 limitations), and the paper never states random assignment, so criterion 1 fails. 385 people analyzed (97/98/93/97), and AUT originality (OCSAI) and GPT-4 story ratings are scored on the output. Design is quasi_people (non-random assignment of people to AI feedback), which the dataset folds into observational context.

one_line_finding: Across batch-assigned conditions, AUT originality rose from pre to post in all four arms (e.g., F/CL 2.56 to 2.81, NF/CL 2.63 to 2.84), and the only significant post-training arm difference favored no feedback over feedback under adaptive difficulty (NF/VL vs F/VL, DeltaM = 0.175, SE = 0.06, d = 0.41; pp. 13-14).
open_questions: Assignment: the paper says 'between-subject design' but describes batch recruitment per condition; confirm no random assignment is stated anywhere (OSF materials not checked).
The printed p-value for the post-training one-way ANOVA (F(3, 381) = 3.34, p = 0.002) looks inconsistent with F = 3.34 on (3, 381) df; recorded as printed (p. 13).

Page 16 cites Figure 4 for GPT-evaluated story scores and p. 24 cites Figure 4 for the GPT vs self-rated correspondence, but Figure 4 shows AUT fluency; no figure or statistic for the story scores by arm is in the PDF.

Which feedback arm is primary: the AI's role is post-hoc feedback and difficulty selection, not content generation; F/CL vs NF/CL is the cleanest feedback contrast. NF/VL involves AI only through difficulty selection.

AI availability for story ratings (S1-O3) is coded 'mixed': feedback arrives after each story, so stories in rounds 2-5 follow AI feedback but are written without AI help; round 1 and the NF arms have no AI content.
notes: Self-reported outcomes left out of the outcome list because they are not scored on the output: self-rated creativity of each story (mixed ANOVA round F(4, 1524) = 6.34, condition F(3, 381) = 3.38, interaction F(12, 1524) = 0.16, p. 16), perceived task difficulty (pp. 10-11), fatigue (p. 11), usefulness ratings of suggestion themes (Figure 7, p. 19), and qualitative reflections (pp. 17-20). Difficulty-level progression is compared between VL arms with chi-square tests (p. 13). No diversity or homogenization outcome is measured. The PDF page numbers match the printed 'x of 31' numbers.
